blueprint_concepts: Family of lines through the intersection of two lines
english: Consider the family of planes $(4x+4y+7z-4)+\lambda(2x+3y+2z-1)=0$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. Each plane of this family meets the $xy$-plane in a line. Let $\Pi$ be the plane of the family whose line of intersection with the $xy$-plane is at the greatest distance from the point $(5,3,0)$. Then the cosine of the acute angle between $\Pi$ and the $xy$-plane is ______.
hindi: समतलों के कुल $(4x+4y+7z-4)+\lambda(2x+3y+2z-1)=0$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ पर विचार कीजिए। इस कुल का प्रत्येक तल $xy$-तल को एक रेखा में काटता है। माना कि $\Pi$ इस कुल का वह तल है जिसकी $xy$-तल के साथ प्रतिच्छेदन रेखा बिन्दु $(5,3,0)$ से अधिकतम दूरी पर है। तब $\Pi$ तथा $xy$-तल के बीच के न्यून कोण की कोज्या (cosine) ______ है।
solution: On $z=0$: $(4x+4y-4)+\lambda(2x+3y-1)=0$, a family of lines through the intersection $M$ of $x+y=1$ and $2x+3y=1$: $M=(2,-1)$
Distance of $Q(5,3)$ from a line through $M$ is at most $QM=5$, with equality for the line through $M$ perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{MQ}=(3,4)$: $3x+4y-2=0$
solution_full: Putting $z=0$, the plane of the family meets the $xy$-plane in the line $(4x+4y-4)+\lambda(2x+3y-1)=0$, i.e. $(4+2\lambda)x+(4+3\lambda)y-(4+\lambda)=0$. (The coefficients of $x$ and $y$ never vanish together, since $4+2\lambda=0$ gives $\lambda=-2$ and then $4+3\lambda=-2\neq0$; so each member is a genuine line.)
These lines form the family of lines through the point of intersection of $x+y-1=0$ and $2x+3y-1=0$: subtracting twice the first from the second gives $y=-1$, so $x=2$ and $M=(2,-1)$.

For any line through $M$, its distance from $Q(5,3)$ is $QM\,|\sin\phi|\le QM$, where $\phi$ is the angle between the line and $MQ$. $QM=\sqrt{9+16}=5$, and equality holds only for the line through $M$ perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{MQ}=(3,4)$, namely $3(x-2)+4(y+1)=0$, i.e. $3x+4y-2=0$.

This line belongs to the family when $\dfrac{4+2\lambda}{3}=\dfrac{4+3\lambda}{4}$, i.e. $16+8\lambda=12+9\lambda$, so $\lambda=4$; then $(4+2\lambda,\ 4+3\lambda,\ -(4+\lambda))=(12,16,-8)=4(3,4,-2)$, as required.
The angle between $\Pi$ and the $xy$-plane is the angle between their normals $(12,16,15)$ and $(0,0,1)$: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{144+256+225}}=\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{625}}=\dfrac{15}{25}=0.6$.
originality_note: New: the traces of a family of planes on the xy-plane form a family of lines through a fixed point; the two-dimensional extremal property of that pencil (farthest line from a point is perpendicular to the joining segment) selects the plane, whose inclination is then asked (way 5: the link between the two families is the discovery). Closest known: the line of a family through a fixed point at maximum distance from a given point (2D); plane through the line of intersection satisfying a condition (3D). Different because: the 2D extremal problem is hidden inside the 3D family through its traces.

concept_use.Family of planes: The planes P1 + lambda P2 = 0 through the line of intersection of the two given planes; lambda = 4 picks Pi and its normal (12, 16, 15).
concept_use.Family of lines through the intersection: The traces on z = 0 form the family of lines L1 + lambda L2 = 0 through M(2, -1); the farthest one from (5, 3) is perpendicular to MQ.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, plane, vector and parameter is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that no member is parallel to the xy-plane (so every trace is a line), that the maximum distance 5 is attained only at lambda = 4 (sampled lambda in [-20, 20]), and that the acute angle has cosine 0.6. Changed: no change.
key_step: Reducing the 3D family to its traces on z = 0, a family of lines through M, and using the farthest-line property.
justification: Two ideas from different chapters must be linked (family of planes and the extremal line of a pencil), followed by a routine angle computation. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q6 (L3), a plane through a line with a further condition; numerical format.
